A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Concept-as-Tree work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original personalization benchmarks, ablations, sample-diversity analyses and a human evaluation, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and human-evaluation results, and additionally reports computational-cost estimates and qualitative sample examples.

M1.justification: The concept-tree construction, self-refinement, editing operations, multi-concept merging, diffusion generation and PCS filtering remain unchanged. New Appendix B explains the existing framework without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use MyVLM, Yo’LLaVA and MC-LLaVA with the same recognition, choice, VQA and captioning tasks, including single- and multi-concept settings. Figure 26 illustrates existing concept categories without adding a dataset or evaluation domain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same participating methods, including GPT-4o+Prompt and RAP-MLLM. The filtering comparisons also retain None, cosine similarity, PCS, CLIP, DINOv2, combined encoders and GPT-4o in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: The benchmark splits, metrics, real/synthetic-data controls and LLaVA-1.5-13B backbone remain unchanged. The new cost paragraph documents workload and hardware details without establishing a revision to those experiments; Table 1 moves existing metric definitions into its caption.

E4.justification: Figure 26 adds a small qualitative comparison showing how synthetic positive, hard-negative and easy-negative samples relate to reference images for three concepts. Existing quantitative ablations and human evaluation are retained; v3’s appendix filtering and data-component analyses are relocated into v4 Section 4.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental results. Existing distribution summaries are unchanged, and v4’s approximate timings do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All seven matched numerical result tables retain identical entries. New Appendix B reports approximately 240 seconds for diffusion tuning, 400 seconds for synthesis and 60 seconds for QA generation, totaling 700 seconds per concept, alongside a 3,600-second personalization comparison. Figure 26 adds qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: The tree definitions, dataset construction, editing equations and PCS mathematics are unchanged. The encoder equation moves inline and cosine similarity is renumbered from Equation 5 to Equation 4; no theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the claims of controllable concept-tree synthesis, PCS filtering, personalization improvements and operation with 1–3 reference images. The stated scientific scope and principal novelty claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly characterizes CaT as a framework for managing diverse prompts, including flat, structured and scene-graph-like representations. It also argues that the reported synthesis overhead is acceptable relative to personalization training. Existing result interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 promises code release; v4 states release and supplies a repository URL. Appendix B newly specifies A100 hardware and parallelism, three reference images, 630 generated images with threefold filtering, 300 QA pairs and component timings. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed benchmark training.

R1.justification: Appendix B explicitly explains the relationship to SSD-LLM and why it is not directly compared for customized synthesis. Citations add works including M2A, Jarvis and Pearl, while removing LLM for Data Management. The data-quality related-work discussion is largely relocated from the appendix.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: supplementary data-quality related work moves into Section 2, two appendix ablations move into Section 4.3, a new explanatory Appendix B is inserted, and references move after the appendices. Most underlying prose is retained, with limited wording, affiliation and terminology edits.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes single-column, extensively resizing and relocating figures, tables and prompt boxes. Tables are reordered, Table 1’s metric labels move into its caption, diagram labels are corrected, and Figure 26 is added. Existing plots retain their reported content.

improvement.justification: v4 provides a concrete code URL, useful runtime and hardware disclosure, clearer attribution to SSD-LLM, and more accessible placement of existing ablations. These improve transparency and explanation while benchmark evidence remains unchanged. The new timing comparison uses a 7B model despite the retained 13B benchmark setup, limiting its direct applicability.
